newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on setback, spreading.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on setback, spreading.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed lower on a setback, especially in soymeal, after the strong rallies during mid-week, traders said.
Position rolling by Rosenthal Collins was featured in CBOT soyoil futures and soymeal was pressured by early unwinding of meal/oil spreads.
Traders said Rosenthal Collins did 3,500 lots of March/May soyoil which probably was rolling out of the firm's short position in the March.
Profit taking was noted in soymeal plus cash merchandisers cited the steep level of cash soymeal.
That scenario was leading end users to buy meal only on a hand-to-mouth basis, cash merchandisers said.

Trading was quiet compared with the previous four sessions this week as the market prepared for the release late Friday of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report. Also trading was subdued before the three day holiday. Futures markets will be closed Monday in observance of the U.S. President's Day holiday.
Soyoil closed 0.09 to 0.20 cent per lb lower, with March down 0.17 at 23.67. Soymeal was $0.60 to $1.80 per ton lower, with March down $0.60 at $248.20.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,000 contracts, below the 23,523 traded Thursday. Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, below the 16,491 traded Thursday.
